public_rationale: The April 9, 2026 preprint reports GPU-accelerated scientific computation, including benefits to a 2025 tsunami-forecasting application [e1]. Civo's August 6, 2026 discussion describes non-AI workloads and hardware tradeoffs, but falls after the May 2026 target period [e2]. Neither source measures the breadth, capacity share or economic significance of non-AI use across AI-oriented GPU facilities in May 2026, so neither narrow nor substantial alternative usefulness is established [e1, e2].
limitations: The scientific applications in e1 do not establish representative deployment across AI-oriented facilities.
The later provider discussion in e2 supplies no May 2026 workload shares or measured facility economics.
The claim supplies no threshold for 'very little else.'

from_speaker: An AI data center full of AI GPUs
useful for AI and very little else

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns practical usefulness outside AI, including economic and operational suitability, rather than whether another program can technically execute.
The explicit acknowledgment of analytics, modeling and science means isolated examples in those fields do not automatically contradict the claim.
I use May 2026, the latest completed calendar month before the post, as the reference period for this ongoing technical state. This is an evaluator-selected reporting window.
Evidence must address AI-oriented GPU facilities, rather than treating every graphics card or purpose-built scientific supercomputer as interchangeable.
criteria.support_condition: Representative workload and deployment evidence shows that practical non-AI uses of the relevant GPU facilities were narrow and economically marginal during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative deployment evidence shows substantial, practically viable non-AI uses across the relevant AI-oriented GPU facilities during the target period.
